parts.text: יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵינוּ מַלְאָכִים הֲמוֹנֵי מַעְלָה. עִם עַמְּךָ יִשְׂרָאֵל קְבוּצֵי מַטָּה: יַחַד כֻּלָּם קְדֻשָּׁה לְךָ יְשַׁלֵּשׁוּ כַּדָּבָר הָאָמוּר עַל יַד נְבִיאֶךָ וְקָרָא זֶה אֶל זֶה וְאָמַר: <small>קו"ח:</small>
קָדוֹשׁ קָדוֹשׁ קָדוֹשׁ יְהֹוָה צְבָאוֹת מְלֹא כָל הָאָרֶץ כְּבוֹדוֹ:
כְּבוֹדוֹ מָלֵא עוֹלָם. מְשָׁרְתָיו שׁוֹאֲלִים זֶה לָזֶה אַיֵּה מְקוֹם כְּבוֹדוֹ לְהַעֲרִיצוֹ. לְעֻמָּתָם מְשַׁבְּחִים וְאוֹמְרִים:
מִמְּקוֹמוֹ הוּא יִפֶן בְּרַחֲמָיו לְעַמּוֹ. וְיָחוֹן עַם הַמְיַחֲדִים שְׁמוֹ עֶרֶב וָבוֹקֶר בְּכָל יוֹם תָּמִיד. פַּעֲמַיִם בְּאַהֲבָה שְׁמַע אוֹמְרִים:
שְׁמַע יִשְׂרָאֵל יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵינוּ יְהֹוָה אֶחָד:

הוּא אֱלֹהֵינוּ הוּא אָבִינוּ. הוּא מַלְכֵּנוּ הוּא מוֹשִׁיעֵנוּ. וְהוּא יוֹשִׁיעֵנוּ וְיִגְאָלֵנוּ שֵׁנִית וְיַשְׁמִיעֵנוּ בְּרַחֲמָיו שֵׁנִית לְעֵינֵי כָּל חַי לֵאמֹר. הֵן גָּאַלְתִּי אֶתְכֶם אַחֲרִית כְּרֵאשִׁית לִהְיוֹת לָכֶם לֵאלֹהִים:
יִמְלֹךְ יְהֹוָה לְעוֹלָם. אֱלֹהַיִךְ צִיּוֹן לְדֹר וָדֹר. הַלְלוּיָהּ:</small></small></small>

parts.text: יִשְׂמְחוּ בְמַלְכוּתְךָ שׁוֹמְרֵי שַׁבָּת וְקוֹרְאֵי עוֹנֶג עַם מְקַדְּשֵׁי שְׁבִיעִי. כֻּלָּם יִשְׂבְּעוּ וְיִתְעַנְּגוּ מִטּוּבֶךָ. וּבַשְּׁבִיעִי רָצִיתָ בּוֹ וְקִדַּשְׁתּוֹ חֶמְדַת יָמִים אוֹתוֹ קָרָאתָ. זֵכֶר לְמַעֲשֵׂה בְרֵאשִׁית:</small></small>

וְהַשִּׂיאֵנוּ יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵינוּ אֶת בִּרְכַּת מוֹעֲדֶיךָ. לְחַיִּים טוֹבִים וּלְשָׁלוֹם. לְשִׂמְחָה וּלְשָׂשׂוֹן. כַּאֲשֶׁר רָצִיתָ וְאָמַרְתָּ לְבָרְכֵנוּ: (לשבת אֱלֹהֵינוּ וֵאלֹהֵי אֲבוֹתֵינוּ רְצֵה נָא בִמְנוּחָתֵנוּ:)
</small> קַדְּשֵׁנוּ בְּמִצְוֹתֶיךָ וְתֵן חֶלְקֵנוּ בְּתוֹרָתֶךָ שַׂבְּעֵנוּ מִטּוּבֶךָ וְשַׂמַּח נַפְשֵׁנוּ בִּישׁוּעָתֶךָ. וְטַהֵר לִבֵּנוּ לְעָבְדְּךָ בֶּאֱמֶת. וְהַנְחִילֵנוּ יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵינוּ.
</small>מוֹעֲדֵי קָדְשֶׁךָ וְיִשְׂמְחוּ בְךָ יִשְׂרָאֵל מְקַדְּשֵׁי שְׁמֶךָ: בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְהֹוָה מְקַדֵּשׁ

parts.text: וְתֵעָרֵב לְפָנֶיךָ עֲתִירָתֵנוּ כְּעוֹלָה וּכְקָרְבָּן. אָנָא רַחוּם. בְּרַחֲמֶיךָ הָרַבִּים. הָשֵׁב שְׁכִינָתְךָ לְצִיּוֹן עִירְךָ וְסֵדֶר הָעֲבוֹדָה לִירוּשָׁלָיִם. וְתֶחֱזֶינָה עֵינֵינוּ בְּשׁוּבְךָ לְצִיּוֹן בְּרַחֲמִים. וְשָׁם נַעֲבָדְךָ בְּיִרְאָה כִּימֵי עוֹלָם וּכְשָׁנִים קַדְמוֹנִיּוֹת:
בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְהֹוָה. שֶׁאוֹתְךָ לְבַדְּךָ בְּיִרְאָה נַעֲבֹד:

parts.text: אִם תָּשִׁיב מִשַּׁבָּת רַגְלֶךָ עֲשׂוֹת חֲפָצֶךָ בְּיוֹם קָדְשִׁי. וְקָרָאתָ לַשַּׁבָּת עֹנֶג לִקְדוֹשׁ יְהֹוָה מְכֻבָּד. וְכִבַּדְתּוֹ מֵעֲשׂוֹת דְּרָכֶיךָ מִמְּצוֹא חֶפְצְךָ וְדַבֵּר דָּבָר: אָז תִּתְעַנַּג עַל יְהֹוָה וְהִרְכַּבְתִּיךָ עַל בָּמֳתֵי אָרֶץ. וְהַאֲכַלְתִּיךָ נַחֲלַת יַעֲקֹב אָבִיךָ. כִּי פִּי יְהֹוָה דִּבֵּר:

parts.text: וְשָׁמְרוּ בְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת. לַעֲשׂוֹת אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת לְדֹרֹתָם בְּרִית עוֹלָם: בֵּינִי וּבֵין בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אוֹת הִיא לְעוֹלָם כִּי שֵׁשֶׁת יָמִים עָשָׂה יְהֹוָה אֶת הַשָּׁמַיִם וְאֶת הָאָרֶץ. וּבַיּוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי שָׁבַת וַיִּנָּפַשׁ: זָכוֹר אֶת יוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת לְקַדְּשׁוֹ. שֵׁשֶׁת יָמִים תַּעֲבוֹד וְעָשִׂיתָ כָּל מְלַאכְתֶּךָ: וְיוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי שַׁבָּת לַיהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה כָל מְלָאכָה אַתָּה וּבִנְךָ וּבִתֶּךָ עַבְדְּךָ וַאֲמָתְךָ וּבְהֶמְתֶּךָ וְגֵרְךָ אֲשֶׁר בִּשְׁעָרֶיךָ: כִּי שֵׁשֶׁת יָמִים עָשָׂה יְהֹוָה אֶת הַשָּׁמַיִם וְאֶת הָאָרֶץ אֶת הַיָּם וְאֶת כָּל אֲשֶׁר בָּם וַיָּנַח בַּיּוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי: עַל כֵּן בֵּרַךְ יְהֹוָה אֶת יוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת וַיְקַדְּשֵׁהוּ:

he:Holidays/Yom Tov Daytime Kiddush:8.en: When sanctifying in the Sukkah, bless here to dwell in the Sukkah:

he:Holidays/Prayer Upon Entering Sukkah:.en: It is written: 'You shall dwell in booths for seven days'—meaning: you shall dwell in a sukkah as you dwell in your house all year, so now your primary dwelling shall be in the sukkah. When coming from the synagogue, enter the sukkah and recite the blessing immediately. When reciting the blessing to dwell in the sukkah, intend to exempt both the meal and the sleep with this blessing. In the blessing Shehecheyanu, intend that you are blessing for the festival and also for the sukkah. The custom is not to recite the blessing to dwell in the sukkah except for a fixed meal (kovea), and to recite HaMotzi first, then the blessing to dwell in the sukkah before tasting.

parts.text: יְהִי רָצוֹן מִלְּפָנֶיךָ יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהַי וֵאלֹהֵי אֲבוֹתַי שֶׁתַּשְׁרֶה שְׁכִינָתְךָ בֵּינֵינוּ וְתִפְרוֹס עָלֵינוּ סֻכַּת שְׁלוֹמֶךָ בִּזְכוּת מִצְוַת סֻכָּה שֶׁאֲנַחְנוּ מְקַיְּמִין לְיַחְדָא שְׁמָא דְקוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא וּשְׁכִינְתֵּהּ בִּדְחִילוּ וּרְחִימוּ לְיַחֲדָא שֵׁם י"ה בו"ה בְּיִחוּדָא שְׁלִים בְּשֵׁם כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל,
וּלְהַקִּיף אוֹתָם מִזִּיו כְּבוֹדֶךָ הַקָּדוֹשׁ וְהַטָּהוֹר נָטוּי עַל רָאשֵׁיהֶם מִלְּמָעְלָה כְּנֶשֶׁר יָעִיר קִנּוֹ,
</small>. וּבִזְכוּת צֵאתִי מִבֵּיתִי הַחוּצָה וְדֶרֶךְ מִצְוֹתֶיךָ אָרוּצָה יֵחָשֵׁב לִי זֹאת כְּאִלּוּ הִרְחַקְתִּי נְדוֹד,
וּמֵאוּשְׁפִּיזִין עִלָּאִין אוּשְׁפִּיזִין דִּמְהֵימְנוּתָא תִּהְיֶינָה אָזְנֶיךָ קַשּׁוּבוֹת רַב בְּרָכוֹת,
וְלָרְעֵבִים גַּם צְמֵאִים תֶּן לַחְמָם וּמֵימָם הַנֶּאֱמָנִים,
וְתִתֶּן לִי זְכוּת לָשֶׁבֶת וְלַחֲסוֹת בְּסֵתֶר צֵל כְּנָפֶךָ בְּעֵת פְּטִירָתִי מִן הָעוֹלָם,
וּתְהֵא חֲשׁוּבָה מִצְוַת סֻכָּה זוּ שֶׁאֲנִי מְקַיֵּם כְּאִלּוּ קִיַּמְתִּיהָ בְּכָל פְּרָטֶיהָ וְדִקְדּוּקֶיהָ וּתְנָאֶיהָ וְכָל מִצְוֹת הַתְּלוּיִם בָּהּ. וְתֵיטִיב לָנוּ הַחֲתִימָה,
וּתְזַכֵּנוּ לֵישֵׁב יָמִים רַבִּים עַל הָאֲדָמָה אַדְמַת קֹדֶשׁ בַּעֲבוֹדָתֶךָ וּבְיִרְאָתֶךָ: בָּרוּךְ יְהֹוָה לְעוֹלָם אָמֵן וְאָמֵן:</small>

he:Holidays/Prayer Upon Entering Sukkah:.en: On the first night, upon entering the sukkah before sitting to eat, and on every day before the meal, say this:
In the book Yesod Yosef, it is written to recite this prayer at that time:

he:Nissan/The'Nasi' Readings:1.en: Order of the Month of Nissan

he:Nissan/The'Nasi' Readings:3.en: In the month of Nissan, it is customary to read the portion of the Princes. On the 1st of Nissan, one begins from the portion of the Priestly Blessing until Nachshon ben Aminadav; on the 12th of the month, one reads the prince and 'This was the dedication of the altar' until 'Thus was the work of the lampstand.'

he:Nissan/Search for Hametz:1.en: Order for the Search for Chametz

he:Nissan/Search for Hametz:2.en: On the night before Erev Pesach, one searches for chametz. One must search at the very beginning of the night; it is forbidden to begin eating or doing any work half an hour before nightfall.

he:Nissan/Search for Hametz:3.en: Some have the custom to place crumbs of bread in places where the searcher will find them, out of concern that if nothing is found, the blessing would be in vain. The custom is to place ten crumbs. It is clear that one who does not search properly but merely gathers these crumbs has not fulfilled the mitzvah of searching and has recited a blessing in vain.

he:Nissan/Search for Hametz:4.en: Before searching for chametz, one says this:

he:Nissan/Search for Hametz:8.en: One searches for chametz by the light of a candle. Immediately after the search, one nullifies the chametz and says:

he:Nissan/Search for Hametz:10.en: If one does not understand the Aramaic, one may nullify the chametz in a language one understands, in Hebrew or in a foreign language. After the search, one must be careful with the chametz set aside for hiding.

he:Nissan/Burning Hametz:2.en: On the 14th of Nissan, until the end of the fifth hour, one nullifies chametz a second time. It is preferable to nullify it after burning the chametz, so that the mitzvah of burning is fulfilled with one's own chametz. One should make a separate fire, burn the chametz, and say:

he:Nissan/Burning Hametz:3.en: I am ready and prepared to fulfill the positive and negative commandments of burning chametz for the sake of the holy union of the Holy One, Blessed be He, and His Shekhinah, through the Hidden and Concealed One, in the name of all Israel:

he:Nissan/Burning Hametz:4.en: May the favor of the Lord, our God, be upon us; may He establish the work of our hands upon us; may He establish the work of our hands.

he:Nissan/Burning Hametz:5.en: All chametz and leaven that are in my domain, that I have seen and that I have not seen, that I have touched and that I have not touched, that I have removed and that I have not removed, are nullified and ownerless like the dust of the earth.

he:Nissan/Burning Hametz:6.en: May it be Your will, Lord our God and God of our fathers, just as I am removing chametz from my house and domain, so may the Lord, my God and the God of my fathers, remove all the outsiders and the spirit of impurity from the land, and remove our evil inclination from us, and grant us a heart of flesh. May all the other side and all wickedness be consumed like smoke, and may the dominion of violence be removed from the land, and may all who oppress the Shekhinah be consumed by a spirit of burning and a spirit of judgment, just as You consumed Egypt and their gods in those days and in this time. Amen.

he:Nissan/Pesach Offering:1.en: Order of Reciting the Pesach Offering

he:Nissan/Pesach Offering:2.en: In times when the Temple stood, the Pesach was slaughtered on the 14th of Nisan after the afternoon Tamid. Therefore, it is fitting for those who fear and tremble at the word of God to engage in the order of the Pesach offering after Mincha, which corresponds to the afternoon Tamid. This is the order:

he:Nissan/Pesach Offering:5.en: The Gaon Maharilbats zt"l strongly objected to reciting the order of the Pesach offering as found in the daily siddur, and stated that it should be recited as follows:

parts.text: כַּךְ הָיְתָה עֲבוֹדַת קָרְבַּן פֶּסַח בְּאַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר בְּנִיסָן,
אֵין שׁוֹחֲטִין אוֹתוֹ אֶלָא אַחַר תָּמִיד שֶׁל בֵּין הָעַרְבַּיִם,
עֶרֶב פֶּסַח בֵּין בְּחוֹל בֵּין בְּשַׁבָּת הָיָה הַתָּמִיד נִשְׁחַט בְּשֶׁבַע וּמֶחֱצָה,
וְאִם חָל עֶרֶב פֶּסַח לִהְיוֹת עֶרֶב שַׁבָּת הָיוּ שׁוֹחֲטִין אוֹתוֹ בְּשֵׁשׁ וּמֶחֱצָה וְקָרֵב בְּשֶׁבַע וּמֶחֱצָה וְהַפֶּסַח אַחֲרָיו,
כָּל אָדָם מִיִשְׂרָאֵל אֶחָד הָאִישׁ וְאֶחָד הָאִשָׁה בְּנֵי בֵּיתוֹ הַגְדוֹלִים וְהַטְהוֹרִים וְנִמוּלִים <small>(וּכְּשֵׁם שֶׁמִילָתוֹ מְעַכֶּבֶת מִלַעֲשׂוֹת הַפָּסַח וּמִלֶאֱכוֹל בּוֹ,
כַּךְ מִילַת בָּנָיו הַקְטַנִים וּמִילַת עֲבָדָיו בֵּין גְדוֹלִים בֵּין קְטַנִים וּטְבִילַת אִמָהוֹתָיו מְעַכֶּבֶת)</small>
כָּל שֶׁיָכוֹל לְהַגִיעַ לִיְרוּשָׁלַיִם בִּשְׁעַת שְׁחִיטַת הַפֶּסַח חַיָב בְּקָרְבַּן פֶּסַח: </small>
מְבִיאוֹ מִן הַכְּבָשִׂים אוֹ מִן הָעִזִים זָכָר תָּמִים בֶּן שָׁנָה (אֵינוֹ טָעוּן סְמִיכָה)
וְשׁוֹחֲטוֹ בְּכָל מָקוֹם בָּעֲזָרָה אַחַר גְמַר עֲבוֹדַת תָּמִיד הָעֶרֶב וְאַחַר הַטָבַת הַנֵרוֹת,
וְאֵין שׁוֹחֲטִין הַפֶּסַח וְלֹא זוֹרְקִין הַדָּם וְלֹא מַקְטִירִין הַחֵלֶב עַל הַחָמֵץ
<small>(אֲפִילוּ הָיָה כַּזַיִת בִּרְשׁוּתוֹ שֶׁל אֶחָד מִבְּנֵי הַחֲבּוּרָה בִּשְׁעַת אַחַת מֵהָעֲבוֹדוֹת שֶׁל קָרְבַּן פֶּסַח,
</small> וְקִבֵּל דָּמוֹ כֹּהֵן שֶׁבְּרֹאשׁ הַשּׁוּרָה בִּכְלִי שָׁרֵת וְנוֹתֵן לְחֲבֵירוֹ,
כֹּהֵן הַקָרוֹב אֵצֶל הַמִזְבֵּחַ זוֹרְקוֹ זְרִיקָה אַחַת כְּנֶגֶד הַיְסוֹד וְחוֹזֵר הַכְּלִי רֵיקָן לְחֲבֵירוֹ וְחֲבֵירוֹ לְחֲבֵירוֹ,
מְקַבֵּל אֶת הַמָלֵא וּמַחֲזִיר אֶת הָרֵיקָן,
וְהָיוּ הַכֹּהֲנִים עוֹמְדִים שׁוּרוֹת וּבִיְדֵיהֶם בָּזִיכִין שֶׁכּוּלָן כֶּסֶף אוֹ כּוּלָן זָהָב וְלֹא הָיוּ מְעוּרָבִים,
וְלֹא הָיוּ לְבָּזִיכִין שׁוּלַיִם שֶׁלֹּא יַנִיחוּם וְיִקָרֵשׁ הַדָּם,
אַחַר כַּךְ תּוֹלִין אֶת הַפֶּסַח בְּאוּנְקְלָיוֹת
<small>(אוֹ בְּמַקְלוֹת דַקִים מֵנִיחַ עַל כִּתְפוֹ וְעַל כֶּתֶף חֲבֵירוֹ,
<small>(וּבְּשַׁבָּת עַד הַחָזֶה וּמִשָּׁם לְמַטָה שָׁקַל לֵיה בְּבַּרְזָא)</small>
וְקוֹרְעִין בִּטְנוֹ וּמוֹצִיאִין אֵימוּרִים הַחֵלֶב שֶׁעַל הַכֶּרֶס וְיוֹתֶרֶת הַכָּבֵד וּשְׁתֵּי הַכְּלָיוֹת וְחֵלֶב שֶׁעַלֵיהֶן וְהָאַלְיָה,
אִם הָיָה מִמִין הַכְּבָשִׂים לְעוּמַת הֶעָצֶה,
נוֹתֵן בִּכְלִי שָׁרֵת וּמוֹלְחָן וּמַקְטִירָן הַכֹּהֵן עַל הַמַעֲרָכָה,
אֲבָל אִם חָל עֶרֶב פֶּסַח בְּשַׁבָּת מַקְטִירִין וְהוֹלְכִין כָּל הַלַיְלָה,
וּמוֹצִיא קְרָבָיו וּמְמַחֶה אוֹתָן עַד שֶׁמֵסִיר מֵהֶן הַפֶּרֶשׁ
שְׁחִיטָתוֹ וּזְרִיקַת דָמוֹ וּמִיחוּי קְרָבָיו וְהֶקְטֵר חֲלָבָיו דוֹחִין אֶת הַשַׁבָּת,
אִם גָמְרוּ קוֹדֶם שֶׁיַקְרִיבוּ אֶת כֻּלָם,
עַל כָּל קְרִיאָה תָּקְעוּ הֵרִיעוּ וְתָּקְעוּ,
נִכְנְסָה כַּתְּ שְׁנִיָה נָעֲלוּ דַלְתוֹת הָעֲזָרָה,
אַחַר שֶׁיָצְאוּ כֻּלָן רוֹחֲצִין הָעֲזָרָה מֵלִכְלוּכֵי הַדָּם וַאֲפִילוּ בְּשַׁבָּת,

שֶׁכְּשֶׁרוֹצִין לְהָדִיחַ הַרִצְפָּה סוֹתְמִין מְקוֹם יְצִיאַת הַמַיִם וְהִיא מִתְמַלְאָה עַל כָּל גְדוֹתֶיהָ עַד שֶׁהַמַיִם עוֹלִין וְצָפִין וּמְקַבְּצִין אֲלֵיהֶם כָּל דַּם וְלִכְלוּךְ שֶׁבָּעֲזָרָה,
אַחַר כַּךְ פּוֹתְחִין הַסְתִּימָה וְיוֹצְאִין הַמַיִם עִם הַלִכְלוּךְ,
יָצְאוּ כָּל אֶחָד עִם פִּסְחוֹ <small>(וְעוֹר שֶׁלוֹ)</small>
כֵּיצַד צוֹלִין אוֹתוֹ מְבִיאִין שְׁפּוּד שֶׁל רִמוֹן תּוֹחֲבוֹ מִתּוֹךְ פִּיו עַד בֵּית נְקוּבָתוֹ,
וְתּוֹלֶּה כְּרָעָיו וּבְנֵי מֵעָיו חוּצָה לוֹ. וְאֵין מְנַקְרִין אֶת הַפֶּסַח כִּשְׁאָר בָּשָׂר,
בְּשַׁבָּת אֵין מוֹלִיכִין אֶת הַפֶּסַח לְבֵיתָם,
אֶלָא כַּתְּ הָרִאשׁוֹנָה יוֹצְאִין בְּפִּסְחֵיהֶן וְיוֹשְׁבִין בְּהַר הַבַּיִת,
הַשְׁנִיָה יוֹצְאִין עִם פִּסְחֵיהֶן וְיוֹשְׁבִין בְּחֵיל,

he:Nissan/Pesach Offering:11.en: One who fears and trembles at the word of God must recite this at its proper time, so that the recitation takes the place of the offering. He should grieve over the destruction of the Temple and pray before God, Creator of the World, that He build it speedily in our days. Amen.

he:Nissan/Letter of Rav Shimshon of Ostr.en: Letter of Rabbi Shimshon of Ostropol
A wonderful charm to read on Erev Pesach:

Copy from the holy writings of the Kabbalist Rabbi Shimshon of Ostropol: A great and awesome secret. It is written that anyone who contemplates this wonderful and awesome secret properly, even once a year, and especially on Erev Pesach, is assured to be saved that year from all obstacles and unusual death, no one will rule over him, all his enemies will fall before him, and he will tread upon their necks. He will succeed in all his endeavors and profit in all his business until the coming of the Redeemer. Amen, Selah.

Peace to the rabbis of the land, those who build a fence and stand in the breach. May God save them from destruction and ruin. All are holy in the land, each according to his name, questioning and answering. Amen, Selah. In the final analysis, what the Ari z"l wrote in his booklet called "Many Wonders" in the gate called "The Exodus from Egypt," Chapter 3, page 42a, and this is his wording:

Behold, I have already informed you that Pharaoh was struck in Egypt with these ten plagues by three thousand two hundred and eighty angels of destruction, who are stationed in three impure heavens. The first is called Shara, the second is called Tamuk, and the third is called Bisha. Over them is the angel named Delfekt, and over them and all of them is the angel named Taka. In the beginning, it is deficient by thirteen from the third, deficient by six from the fourth, and deficient by six from the ninth, as written:

Behold, the Egyptians were struck in Egypt with ten plagues, and at the sea they were struck with fifty plagues. The name Shpo, by which David ben Yishai held, and the name said "and He struck." From the side of the name Tikl, the Egyptians were struck in Egypt with forty plagues, and at the sea they were struck with two hundred plagues, and the name said "and He struck." From the side of the name Ashcha, the Egyptians were struck in Egypt with fifty plagues, and at the sea they were struck with two hundred and fifty plagues. And by what the Holy One, blessed be He, strikes, He heals the exile. What was their sin and what was their transgression, and what was the iniquity that our fathers committed, to be in this iron furnace, until He redeemed them with these names Deb Tza Kshab. Thus ends the words of the Ari z"l.

Behold, my teachers and rabbis, the holy ones of Israel, these matters are wonders, hidden and sealed, closed and no one explains them. And the great ones of Israel have already asked me to explain the words of the Ari z"l, and I did not tell. And out of the great love of my teachers and rabbis, I will reveal this secret that was revealed to me in a dream vision at night, and now I will reveal the matter in an allusion before the honor of his Torah, and He is merciful and will atone:
And this is the matter:

What the Ari z"l wrote that Pharaoh was struck in Egypt with ten plagues, etc., his intention is this: For the masters of practical Kabbalah said that there are three thousand two hundred and eighty angels of destruction who are appointed to strike the wicked and punish them in Gehinnom and purify them of their sins. And on this it is said: "To strike the wicked with a fist," for Agref is an allusion to three thousand two hundred and eighty, and by them Pharaoh the wicked was also struck. And I, the writer, say that this is a wonderful secret as it is written in the count and number:
Blood. Frogs. Lice. Mixed creatures. Pestilence. Boils. Hail. Locusts. Darkness. The plague of the firstborn:

These ten plagues as I wrote them letter by letter, amount to three thousand two hundred and eighty angels of destruction, appointed to purify the wicked, and it is a wonderful plain meaning, an eye has not seen:

Behold, the calculation is exact as written: Kenem is deficient of a Yod, also Arav is deficient of a Vav. Also Choshech is deficient of a Vav. And then the calculation is exactly, not less and not more than three thousand two hundred and eighty angels of destruction, who punish the wicked. And this is what the Ari z"l wrote:

"As written," meaning as written in the Torah scroll, and not as written in siddurim and in the Haggadah, for there they are all written full. Rather, it must be deficient as written in the Torah scroll. And also Rabbi Yehuda did not write all the signs, only the initials, Datzach Adash BeAhav, as written by Rabbi Isaac Abarbanel and as I wrote above:
And this is what the Ari z"l wrote: "In the beginning deficient from the third thirteen," meaning:

The third plague which is Kenem is deficient of a Yod. "From the fourth six" which is the plague of Arav is also deficient of a Vav. "And deficient from the ninth six," which is the plague of Choshech is also deficient of a Vav. And what he said "as written," he means that so it is written in the Torah scroll deficient, as mentioned above:

And this is the secret of these "ten plagues that the Holy One, blessed be He, brought" in Egypt, exactly three thousand two hundred and eighty angels of destruction who struck Pharaoh and the Egyptians in Egypt, stationed in these three heavens: one called Shara, one called Tamuk, and one called Bisha. Also in this there is a great and wonderful secret, these three thousand two hundred and eighty camps that struck Pharaoh and the Egyptians in Egypt as stated, stationed in these three impure heavens, the verse told us a wonderful and awesome secret, and the Magid corrected it as he taught these "ten plagues that He brought" in these three words are alluded the three impure heavens, and the three thousand two hundred and eighty angels of destruction who struck Pharaoh and the Egyptians in Egypt, as the count of ten plagues:

For this is ten letters Shara, plagues letters Tamuk, that He brought letters Bisha, an allusion to these three impure heavens in which there are stationed as the count of three thousand two hundred and eighty angels of destruction exactly, as the count of ten plagues Blood Frogs etc., and they are the ones who struck Pharaoh and the Egyptians in Egypt, for angels of destruction are stationed to strike the wicked to purify them of their sins as stated. And by their hand He struck Pharaoh and the Egyptians in Egypt the count of these ten plagues, and it is a great wonder:

And what the Ari z"l wrote: "And over them the angel Delfekt," his intention is that this name's root comes from the word of the Egyptians, and it is: that the three heavens are: Esar Mochot SheHavia and as the Gaon explained, and it extends to the Egyptians which is the name Delfekt in the letters preceding the letters of the Egyptians, and the final Mem is the Mem of plurality and is not from the root, and the Magid alluded to this in the saying: "These ten plagues that the Holy One, blessed be He, brought upon the Egyptians in Egypt," meaning the letters that are preceding the letters of the Egyptians:

And what the Ari z"l wrote: "And over them and over all of them the angel named Taka," his intention is that the initials of these ten plagues, Datzach Adash BeAhav, in gematria Taka, as the count of the angel exactly, and as the count of Asher, and this is the secret of the intention of the verse in the portion Bo: "And in order that you may tell in the ear of your son and your son's son what I did to the Egyptians," Asher specifically, which is as the number Taka, and like it many verses thousands, guarded on this for the secret of Asher, as the count of the initials of the ten plagues as we explained, and we have in this wonderful secrets. And the honor of God is to hide the matter:

And what our teacher the Ari z"l wrote: "The name Shpo by which David ben Yishai held, and the name said and He struck them in Egypt ten plagues, and at the sea they were struck fifty plagues. And the name Tikl said and He struck them in Egypt forty plagues, and at the sea they were struck two hundred plagues. And the name Ashcha said and He struck them in Egypt fifty plagues, and at the sea they were struck two hundred and fifty plagues." His intention is to a wonderful and awesome secret:

The dispute of Rabbi Yossi the Galilean and Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Akiva mentioned in the Haggadah. Rabbi Yossi the Galilean says how many, and Rabbi Eliezer says how many, and Rabbi Akiva says how many, and this is what the Ari z"l wrote: And the name Shpo said and He struck them in Egypt ten plagues, and at the sea they were struck fifty plagues, an allusion to Rabbi Yossi the Galilean. For Rabbi Yossi the Galilean in gematria Shpo, and what is written that David ben Yishai held by it, is also an allusion, David ben Yishai gematria name Shpo, that in that name specifically came David ben Yishai. And it is also an allusion to what is written in the book Sodei Raza, that Rabbi Yossi the Galilean is a spark of David ben Yishai. And this name struck them. And from the side of the name Tikl the Egyptians were struck in Egypt forty plagues, and at the sea they were struck two hundred plagues, an allusion to the secret of Rabbi Eliezer in gematria Tikl, and it is Rabbi Eliezer says, specifically, that it is the name Tikl, the Egyptians were struck in Egypt forty plagues, and at the sea they were struck two hundred plagues. And what is written the name Ashcha struck in Egypt fifty plagues, and at the sea they were struck two hundred and fifty plagues, an allusion to the secret of Rabbi Akiva, which is in gematria Ashcha with the inclusive, that this name said that the Egyptians were struck in Egypt fifty plagues, and at the sea they were struck two hundred and fifty plagues. Behold these three names Shpo Tikl Ashcha allude to these three Tannaim:

Rabbi Yossi the Galilean in gematria Shpo, Rabbi Eliezer in gematria Tikl, Rabbi Akiva in gematria Ashcha, and it is a wonderful and awesome secret. Secret of secrets. Hidden of hidden. It is as I wrote to the honor of his Torah, and He is merciful and will atone sin:

And what our teacher the Ari z"l wrote: "By what the Holy One, blessed be He, strikes, He heals the exile, what was their sin what was their transgression of our fathers" etc., his intention: In these ten plagues which are Datzach Adash BeAhav, are alluded in these letters the secret and reason of the descent of our fathers to Egypt, as I wrote to the honor of his Torah. And behold in these plagues He struck them, and the Holy One, blessed be He, will heal us and strike them a great blow, the finger of God it is, and from the blow itself comes healing for Israel, that the Holy One, blessed be He, redeemed them, and as I wrote.

And what is written: "What was their sin" etc., he means: In these plagues is alluded the sin of our fathers that caused the descent to Egypt. And we have a wonderful and awesome secret to resolve this difficulty that the honor of their Torah asked of me, but also this is clear as I wrote to their honor, wonders from his holy and pure Torah.

And what the Ari z"l wrote: "That the Holy One, blessed be He, redeemed us with these names Deb Tza Kshab," his intention is that the first letters of Datzach Adash BeAhav are Deb, and the second letters are Tza, and the last letters are Kshab, and are alluded in these three names the healing that the Holy One, blessed be He, healed Israel, that He redeemed us with them, behold in those plagues that they struck the Egyptians, are alluded the redemption and healing for Israel. And may it be acceptable before the Holy One, blessed be He, that He show us the coming of our Messiah speedily in our days, with the angels attached to the redemption, and fulfill in us the verse written: As in the days of your going out from the land of Egypt I will show you wonders, Amen, victory, Selah:
End of the copy:
